Document projections

A document projection selects finite graph data and produces typed blocks. A renderer encodes those blocks as Markdown, HTML or plain text.

Contract illustration
ProjectionDocumentDiff
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
Block and row identities are stable and separate from display order. Document patches describe structural changes before rendering.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
The renderer produces output text. Editing that text requires a separately designed input mapping. Document overflow either rejects the request or marks truncation.

Project and render Markdown

Pass the returned typed snapshot to a renderer. Keep its source revisions.
UsageExamples.cs
public static async Task RenderMarkdownAsync(
    IDocumentProjection projection, IDocumentRenderer renderer,
    ProjectDocument request,
    Func<RenderedDocument, CancellationToken, ValueTask> save,
    Func<DocumentResult, CancellationToken, ValueTask> reportFailure,
    CancellationToken ct)
{
    await foreach (var result in projection.ProjectAsync(One(request, ct), ct))
    {
        if (result.Snapshot is not { } snapshot || !result.Errors.IsEmpty)
        {
            await reportFailure(result, ct);
            continue;
        }
        var render = new RenderDocument(result.Request, snapshot,
            DocumentFormat.Markdown, RendererVersion: "1");
        await foreach (var output in renderer.RenderAsync(One(render, ct), ct))
            await save(output, ct);
    }
    // Snapshot.Sources records the graph versions used. Inspect completeness:
    // explicitly truncated documents remain distinguishable from complete ones.
}
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.
